perplexity.description:
Audioweb's self-titled debut album was originally released in the UK in October 1996. The Manchester-based band crafted a distinctive sound blending hip hop, rock, and reggae influences, reflecting the diverse musical landscape of the mid-1990s. Produced by Kevin Bacon and Jonathan Quarmby with additional programming by the band, the album features a mix of live instrumentation and programming, with notable contributions such as a sample from Wayne Smith's "Saying Goodbye" on the track "Jah".

This album holds a significant place in Audioweb's discography as their first full-length release, establishing their eclectic style and musical identity. It was initially issued on U2's Mother Records label, emphasizing the band's connection to the alternative and indie scenes of the time. While the album did not achieve major commercial success, it received positive critical attention for its innovative fusion of genres and solid musicianship. The 1996 release was later reissued by Demon Records on vinyl and CD, underscoring its enduring appeal among fans of genre-blending British music from the 1990s.
